name: cards
description: Trading cards. A card is a frozen snapshot of somebody — a PLAYER who minted themselves at a `flags.card_mint` terminal, or an NPC/ENEMY struck from world content when a series opened. Players mint because the card system deliberately does not follow anybody around (tracking every player's kit for a collectible would be a hot-path cost), so you walk to a terminal and hand it the moment: this body, this loadout, these numbers, this thing you just said. NPC and enemy rows are static content, so those cards are struck unattended and never go stale. Every text region has a HARD character budget and the builder never truncates — it emits ranked clauses and stops at the first that would cross, because an omitted clause is invisible and a truncated one is a bug the player can see. Condition is spoken as damage on the front ("split at the knuckles") and named as a band on the back. Rarity is common→legendary, stored on the row and never recomputed, plus an admin-only `architect` rank with pool_weight 0 that never rolls and never appears in a pack. Packs are bought from `flags.vends_packs` machines (powered, like everything else), which open as an ATM-style in-browser cabinet panel rather than transacting from a bare verb: ₵250 buys a `card_foil_sleeve` ITEM into your inventory, unopened and holding no result. The cabinet is branded ARCHITECT DRAFT (never the Mint — minting is a player striking their own card, not something a machine sells) and holds nine coils A1–C3, each with its own derived-not-stored stock that runs out and restocks on the game date with no DB write and no tick; you pick the coil you take from, and the panel says plainly that the coil picks your object, not your odds, because sealed sleeves are identical and the roll still happens at the tear. `openpack` (alias `tear`) is where the sleeve is consumed and its contents are revealed. The COIL decides the sleeve: each one on a coil carries a seed fixed when it was loaded (process salt + machine + game date + coil + depth), stored as one integer on its own inventory row and replayed through mulberry32 at the tear, so a player's physical choice genuinely determines the result. The seed never leaves the server, so a sealed sleeve still cannot be read or traded with known contents, and it fixes only the RANKS — the live pool at tear time fills the faces, so a sleeve never goes stale against a pool that grew while it sat in your coat. About one sleeve in twelve is a HOT RUN with triple weight on epic and legendary, derived from the same seed on a separate stream and invisible until the tear (a spottable hot sleeve would just be the sleeve everybody buys). Sleeve SIZE is itself rolled (4/5/6/7, and a 1% nine-card mis-cut), every card but the last rolled against the pool and the last excluding Common — so every sleeve holds at least an Uncommon. Cards reveal worst-to-best, so the pull always builds and the hit always lands last; the client renders that as a foil-tear cinematic with per-rarity reveal animations and synth SFX, and the plain text log is always emitted alongside it so closing the overlay never loses what you pulled. Dupes stack and scrap at the mint. No tick, no hot-path query; the pool is cached behind one writer.

mint.note: Surfaced by the declaration-only specialized action registered under requiredFlag card_mint, and as a PREVIEW action-link on examining the terminal.

buypack.note: Same shape — requiredFlag vends_packs, plus the BUY control on examining the machine. `sleeve` is the alias.

scrap.note: Duplicates are eaten at a mint terminal, not in the street.
